exposed_notes.title: Airline reservation changes: verify scope, fare basis, and confirmation
exposed_notes.body:
For similar airline reservation work, follow an ordered, conditional workflow:
1. Obtain the user ID and reservation ID; retrieve reservation and user details, and verify ownership, itinerary, passengers, cabin, membership, bags, and payment method.
2. If the itinerary seems inconsistent with the user's description, explain the retrieved segments and connection and ask/check before proceeding. Do not treat a connecting itinerary as a direct flight.
3. For cabin changes, check that no segment has already flown and that cabin remains uniform across the reservation. Do not assume one passenger or one segment can be changed independently. If flight status/date checks are needed, verify every segment, not just one.
4. If asked for upgrade price, retrieve relevant fare data and distinguish a supported quote from an estimate. Compare like-for-like current cabin fares and account for the reservation's pricing/kept-flight rules; do not present an unverified calculation as a guaranteed repricing. The past example calculated using recorded economy prices ($122/$127) against searched business fares ($350/$499), although search results also showed economy fares ($125/$139); thus its $1,200 estimate was not fully validated as the applicable fare difference. If the user requires a firm price and tools cannot provide one, state that limitation and stop before changing anything.
5. Before any booking update, list the exact intended changes and obtain explicit affirmative confirmation. If the user declines or sets a cap below an uncertain estimate, do not make the cabin change; offer only separately authorized feasible changes.
6. For bags, check the membership/cabin allowance and current bag count; add only requested bags, with paid-bag count and payment details consistent with the allowance. The policy's allowance is reservation-user based; don't claim a particular bag is assigned to a named passenger unless supported. Obtain confirmation before updating, then report the tool result and explicitly note changes not made.

Past example outcome: reservation YAX4DR stayed economy; after the user confirmed, baggage update returned 2 total bags and 0 paid bags. No upgrade was made. This record alone does not establish any external grading result.

exposed_notes.body:
Past airline-support experience (feedback level: none; correctness not independently verified): For a one-way NYC–Seattle flight, user specified May 20, initially ambiguously then clarified as 2025, economy, no preferred NYC airport, and later no departure before 11 a.m. The agent enumerated airports and tried direct and one-stop searches for JFK, EWR, and LGA; all returned empty. Search calls accepted date, origin, destination, not cabin or departure-time constraints, so these results did not verify availability by class or departure time. The agent appropriately did not claim to have assessed the 11 a.m. constraint and transferred when user explicitly asked for a human; transfer succeeded.
Procedure for similar work: 1) Collect user ID and clarify trip type, endpoints, date/year, cabin, and airport flexibility; resolve past/ambiguous dates before search. 2) Enumerate applicable airports when flexible, and search relevant route options (direct and one-stop) for each. 3) Track returned results per exact query; if double-checking, repeat/expand searches consistently across every applicable airport and do not summarize an unqueried result as checked. 4) Respect tool limitations: if search inputs do not support cabin or time filters, state that results cannot verify those constraints; avoid asserting comprehensive availability from empty or limited responses. 5) If no results, explain the scope of searches and ask about another date/route; if user explicitly requests a human or the issue cannot be handled, transfer and send the required transfer notice only after successful tool transfer. Stop without booking unless suitable flight details are available and user has confirmed the booking details.

For baggage, check allowance from membership, cabin, and passenger count; do not add more than requested, explain any cost, and obtain explicit confirmation before editing. An existing payment_history gift-card entry was used later despite user profile showing that gift card with a different remaining amount; do not assume payment-history total equals available balance. The flight searches returned date:null, so the selected dates were based on query parameters rather than an explicit date field in results. Earlier agent reported a $186 refund based on update result, but no evaluation verified correctness. Policy says cabin must be consistent across all segments, bag allowances are per passenger, and baggage can be added but not removed. No grading details or correctness conclusion available.
